key_cases.case_name: Connor B. ex rel. Vigurs v. Patrick
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the First Circuit
key_cases.holding: The First Circuit affirmed judgment for the state in a systemic foster-care class action, holding the record did not establish a class-wide substantive due process violation or a class-wide failure to maintain individualized case plans under the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act.
key_cases.relevance: The holding shows what quantum of cross-system evidence a systemic non-compliance claim must produce to survive in this circuit.
key_cases.quote: We agree with the district court that this record does not show a class-wide failure to provide documentation in the form of individualized case plans.

key_cases.case_name: Kane v. Commissioner of Department of Health & Human Services
key_cases.holding: The Law Court vacated the Commissioner's substantiation of a foster parent for abuse and neglect, holding that because a substantiation carries life-altering consequences and implicates a fundamental liberty interest, it requires proof of something more than imperfect or deficient parenting.
key_cases.relevance: The decision documents the stigma and tangible-burden consequences of database listing, the exact harms a registry-accountability analysis must measure.
key_cases.quote: a substantiation finding must be based on an understanding that "abuse or neglect" means, for purposes of section 4088(3)(K), something more than imperfect, overly rigid, or even deficient parenting

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act's requirement that a state plan provide for reasonable efforts to prevent removal and enable return creates no privately enforceable right, either implied under the Act or through 42 U.S.C. § 1983.
key_cases.relevance: Any accountability analysis built on federal statutory requirements must account for the absence of a private right of action under this holding.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.
